title: STaSBO: LLM-Guided Strategy Planning and Configuration Selection for Bayesian Optimization
why_read: An LLM-as-meta-controller approach to Bayesian optimization configuration, interesting to ML practitioners doing hyperparameter or black-box optimization but fairly niche.
analysis: Bayesian optimization is widely used for tuning expensive-to-evaluate systems, but choosing the right surrogate model and acquisition function configuration is itself a hard, problem-dependent decision. This paper uses an LLM as a planner that selects and adjusts these configurations over the course of an optimization run, using a memory of past decisions and outcomes. The claimed improvement is measured by average rank across many benchmark tasks compared to 11 baseline strategies. It's a reasonable idea combining LLM reasoning with classical optimization machinery, though the real-world robustness of LLM-driven meta-control is still unproven.
